articleTitle: Predicting The Melting Temperature Of Polymers Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: One crucial factor in polymer material fabrication is its melting temperature, which is key to determining the manufacturing process. However, difficulties have been encountered in finding correlations between the melting temperature and influencing factors. Therefore, machine learning is employed to discern the relationship between polymer structure and its melting temperature. The models used include KNN, SVR, and XGB, as well as deep learning with ANN and NLP. The ability of SMILES and NLP descriptors in describing polymer structures is also examined. The input length of the models varied between 50 and 200. All models produce the most accurate predictions with an input length of 200. KNN and SVR generate relatively stable but consistently low R-squared values, with MAE values above 40. ANN and NLP exhibit high R-squared values in some trials but with low stability and relatively high MAE values. XGBoost consistently produces higher and more stable R2 values. The best-performing XGBoost model is validated using SMILES strings outside the dataset, demonstrating its predictive ability with an MAE of 24.09, deemed sufficient for predicting melting temperatures.

articleTitle: Procedural Low-Poly Buildings using L-System for Turn-based Tactic Game MECH.AI
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: One of the critical visual components in video game creation is 3D asset prototypes, which also require significant effort. A procedural model using the L-system method for making low-poly buildings can address this issue. This model produces low-poly buildings based on simple parameters input by the user. The model receives input in the form of axioms, which are then processed according to predetermined L-system rules. After the building is formed, it is saved as a prefab in Unity so that it can be reused and modified by the user. The proposed method is implemented to our turn-based tactic MECH.AI and provided as a Unity package (add-on). Experimental results show that the buildings generated by the model have a minimalistic yet functional benefits.

articleTitle: Proposing Tap-Track Platform for Facilitating Implementation of Button-Driven Smart Services
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: In recent years, the movement toward a super smart society as a future society is being promoted as Society 5.0. In this movement, smart services [1] have become very diverse, and the burden on users has increased. Therefore, in this paper, we focus on button-driven smart services, and propose a platform " Tap Track " that makes it easy to implement button-driven smart services. In Tap Track, users can create services that run when a button [2] is pressed with no code, and users can assign their desired services to the button. The processing that can be executed when the button is pressed is playing media files, sending commands to external services, and so on. The usage history of the button can be looked back later as a life log. In the case study, we created a weather forecast confirmation service and a life log service using Tap Track and verified its operation.

articleTitle: Optimized Machine Learning Models for Heart Disease Prediction: A Performance Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: This paper presents a performance analysis of optimized machine learning (ML) models used to predict heart disease. The primary aim of this research was to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of early detection and treatment. Our study employed 6 machine learning (ML) models: Discriminant Analysis, Naïve Bayes, Support Vector Machines (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Ensemble, and Neural Networks (NN). These models were fine-tuned using hyperparameter tuning techniques. The dataset used in this study was the Heart Disease dataset provided on the Kaggle website. The dataset was split into train-test data configurations of 90-10, 85-15, 80-20, 75-25, and 70-30 in percentage for model learning and performance evaluation.Our study demonstrates that optimizing the hyperparameters of Support Vector Machines (SVM) resulted in highly accurate predictions of heart disease. This model outperformed other machine learning models across various train-test dataset splits, particularly at configurations of 90-10, 85-15, 80-20, and 75-25. Notably, the model achieved the highest accuracy of 95% in the 85-15 train-test dataset split configuration. These findings offer valuable insights for healthcare professionals, equipping them with reliable tools for early heart disease detection and well-informed decisionmaking. It is crucial to emphasize that these machine learning models should complement decision-making and should not substitute professional medical judgment.

articleTitle: Implement Website Application For Medical Record Using The Prototype Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: As one of the healthcare facilities that provides direct services to patients, Praktik Mandiri Bidan (PMB) Ika Mardiyanti want to give the best service to patients. But, the service process still relies on manual methods. Based on interview, the challenge is difficulties in managing the large number of forms that need to be filled out manually. This study implements a web-based medical record information system. The system consists of some features such as patient menu, medication menu, service menu, medical record menu, billing, and report menu. The method is used in this study is prototype method contains system requirement analysis, rapid design modeling, user interface system creation, and testing system. The system was developed using PHP with Laravel framework, and MySQL as database. Testing method using Blackbox Testing and User Acceptance Testing (UAT) methods. The result show that system manages data effectively, improves the recording process, and enhances efficiency in medical record data report. The result of blackbox testing achieved 100% success rate and UAT reached 99% satisfaction rate, indicating that the system was well-received by user.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of rPPG Algorithms Across Diverse Countries of Origin
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: Heart rate measurement is crucial for assessing physical health. Traditionally, contact-based method such as PPG requiring skin attachment have been predominant. However, these methods have limitations due to their invasive nature. Remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) offers a non-contact alternative that broadens its application possibilities. Yet, current rPPG methods have not been extensively tested across diverse populations, where varying skin pigmentation can affect measurement accuracy. This study aims to determine the most effective rPPG method for extracting heart rate from individuals of diverse origins. Evaluating Chrominance-based (CHROM), Plane Orthogonal to Skin (POS), and GREEN methods using Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), we found that the POS method demonstrated superior predictive accuracy with an RMSE of 8.45, while GREEN showed comparable performance with an RMSE of 8.89 across different country groups.

articleTitle: Rainfall Forecasting Using Hybrid Learning Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: Rainfall is one of the most important meteorological variables. Rainfall has a multiplicity of effects on agriculture, ecosystems and urbanization. The amount of rainfall cannot currently be determined due to climate change. For this reason, in order to mitigate the effects that arise from heavy rainfall, it is crucial to forecast the amount of rainfall. Currently, statistical techniques and machine learning are two of the methods has been used to forecast rainfall. These methods have been successfully to forecast rainfall. However, it still has low accuracy and need more time to forecast because the rainfall influence parameters are time-series and non-linear. This study will employ a hybrid learning technique to resolve the issue. The method used is a combination of two algorithms, namely long short-term memory (LSTM) and particle swarm optimization (PSO), and the prediction system will be evaluated using RMSE and MAE. Time-series and non-linear rainfall data will be overcome by the LSTM algorithm, and uncertain hyperparameter settings in the LSTM method will be overcome by the PSO algorithm. The ideal LSTM algorithm employing PSO optimization yields the following hyperparameter value results: 143 neurons, learning rate of 0.0000840, and 122 epochs in 50 iterations. With the lowest RMSE and MAE values of 18.557095 and 8.972361, respectively, the prediction model's optimal hyperparameter values can forecast the next five days based on the data used.

articleTitle: Motorbike Helmet Usage Detection in Foggy Weather Conditions with Dark Channel Prior and YOLOV8
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: Driving safety is crucial for maintaining road safety, and helmet use by motorcyclists is essential for reducing serious head injuries during accidents. However, compliance with helmet use remains challenging, especially in developing countries. Automatic detection of helmetless motorcyclists is, therefore, a highly relevant topic for traffic surveillance and law enforcement. One significant challenge is detecting helmetless motorcyclists in non-ideal weather conditions, such as fog, which reduces visibility and hinders visual detection. The Dark Channel Prior (DCP) technique enhances visibility in foggy conditions by exploiting the nature of foggy images, where at least one color channel (red, green, or blue) at each pixel has very low intensity. This dehazing process removes fog effects and improves image contrast. YOLOv8, an advanced object detection algorithm, utilizes an optimized convolutional neural network for real-time, high-accuracy detection of various objects, including motorcyclists and helmets. Combining DCP and YOLOv8 can create a robust system for detecting helmetless motorcyclists in various weather conditions, providing a reliable solution for law enforcement and traffic safety. This motorcycle helmet use detection system can be applied to traffic Closed-Circuit Television (CCTV) for Electronic Traffic Law Enforcement (ETLE), to facilitate authorities in enforcing applicable traffic laws.

articleTitle: Improved Vehicle Traffic Detection Using YOLO Algorithm with Brightness and Contrast Adjustment in Low-light Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: This study aims to improve YOLO (You Only Look Once) object detection in low light conditions by improving image quality using techniques such as CLAHE, brightness/contrast adjustment and noise reduction.CLAHE is expected to improve local contrast in the image, while brightness and contrast adjustment will be used to adjust the overall brightness and contrast. Noise reduction will be used to reduce distracting noise in the image. Experiments will be conducted using YOLOv5 and YOLOv8 to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), F1 score and confusion matrix are used to measure the prediction accuracy. The results of the evaluation method using MAPE showed that the manipulated YOLOv5s produced a score of 0.59, which was higher than the raw YOLOv5s which produced a MAPE score of 0.63. The MAPE score for the manipulated YOLOv8s resulted in a score of 0.49 which was better than the MAPE score for the raw YOLOv8s which was 0.52, concluding that the lower the MAPE value, the better the accuracy of YOLO object detection. The F1 score for the enhanced YOLOv5s is 0.12, which is higher than the score for the pre-enhanced YOLOv5s which is 0.10, and for the YOLOv8s the F1 score is 0.19, which is higher than the non-enhanced model which is 0.18. The results suggest that adjusting image brightness, contrast and noise reduction improves target detection in low light conditions.

articleTitle: Recognition of Open and Closed Eye Using Residual Networks For Driver Drowsiness Detection: Original and CLAHE-enhanced Images
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: Residual Network (ResNet) architecture is implemented in camera-based drowsiness detection. ResNet50, ResNet101, ResNet152, ResNet50V2, ResNet101V2 and ResNet152V2 are performed to build the detection models. Moreover, this study also investigates the use of original images and Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) enhanced images as input. The original image processed using ResNet101V2 gives the best accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score and AUC values of 99.13%, 99.13%, 99.13%, 99.13% and 99.95%. This proposed method outperformed the previous studies. Furthermore, this study shows that the image enhancement technique is not required to improve detection performance.

articleTitle: Finite Element Analysis on Blood Vessels: Understanding Clipping Phenomenon
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: Background: Blood vessels clipping is one of medical interventions that could close any blood vessels rupture in several major conditions, such as heart attack and stroke hemorrhage. Besides coil, the aneurysm clip is one of the medical tools for clipping the vessels. In its development, the clip surface has been limited to discuss, while the configuration of the clip surface holds an important factor. Aims: This study aims to design the surface of surgical clip as well as understanding the clipping phenomenon on the intended blood vessels using the finite element method. Shortened Method: The blood vessel was clamped between two surfaces of surgical clips. This analogy was then simulated using finite element study with a set of constraints and load from 1 to 5N. Results: The load and constraint of 1N results in Von Misses Stress (VMS) less than the Young Modulus of the blood vessels material. Conclusion: It can be concluded that the new design of surgical clip’s surface must have final closing force around 1N to avoid any failure during clamping, such as rupture, slicing, and slip. Implication: This study is significantly helping the manufacturer of surgical clip to have further development regarding the surface profile of surgical clips.

articleTitle: Empowering visually impaired learners: A voice-assisted mobile exam app for scribe-free exams
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: This paper delves into the implementation and effectiveness of a mobile application designed as a Voice-Assisted Exam System specifically for visually impaired (partially or fully blind) students in India. Visually Impaired (VI) students depend on scribes to write exams. Such reliance on scribes presents a significant challenge not only for visually impaired students but also for educational institutions. To address this issue, we have developed an innovative mobile application that utilizes recent advancements in natural language understanding and processing, transforming a mobile phone into a powerful Assistive Technology device. The primary objective of the Voice-Assisted Exam Systems app is to minimize or reduce the dependency on scribes, enabling visually impaired students to independently undertake examinations. Our field-testing of the Voice-Assisted Exam System app prototype across four colleges in the state of Maharashtra, India, revealed promising results. The findings indicate that this app holds substantial potential to significantly reduce the need for human assistance. Consequently, it promotes a more inclusive and equitable academic environment. By leveraging this technology, we aim to empower visually impaired students to be independent, enhancing their academic experience and opportunities.

articleTitle: Decoding the Monkey Pox Outbreak: Unsupervised Machine Learning Using Decision Tree
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: The Monkeypox outbreak in Central London in 2022 has posed significant challenges for healthcare practitioners and public health authorities. That is why this research seeks to use unsupervised machine learning to analyze data from 25,000 infected patients. By taking advantage of clustering techniques, including k-means and hierarchical clustering, we will attempt to identify underlying structures and knowledge sources from the information. Ultimately, this work endeavors to provide new valuable information into the dynamics of the outbreak, including spread trends, geographical clustering, and demographic sources of risk. The results might prove invaluable for developing interventions and control measures in any future outbreaks of the monkeypox virus or other infectious diseases.

articleTitle: Prediction of Total Renewable Energy Consumption using Artificial Intelligence Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: The increasing global energy demand and the necessity to combat climate change have underscored the importance of renewable energy sources in sustainable development. This study investigates the application of advanced Artificial Intelligence (AI) approach—Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA), Random Forest, and Support Vector Machine (SVM)—to forecast renewable energy consumption. Using a monthly Total Renewable Energy Consumption dataset from January 1973 to February 2024, sourced from Our World in Data. The research aims to enhance the accuracy of consumption forecasts to aid stakeholders in optimizing resource allocation, infrastructure development, and strategic decision-making. The results show that the SARIMA model is the most accurate in predicting renewable energy consumption. This model has a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) value of 0.0484 and a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.0196, and an R-Squared value of 0.6918. The study concludes that SARIMA is the most effective AI model for forecasting renewable energy consumption, significantly contributing to energy planning and sustainable management practices. This research provides a robust framework for managing the unpredictability of renewable energy data, supporting more informed energy policy and management decisions.

articleTitle: The Impact of Artificial Intelligence in the Creative Industries: Design and Editing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: The rapid development of artificial intelligence has had a significant influence in various ways, one of which is in the creative design and editing industry. The use of AI in the creative sector has multiple impacts and new challenges for the creative industry. AI as a tool can increase the efficiency and productivity of creative workers. However, the rapid development of AI can also cause job displacement, which becomes a challenge for creative workers. Therefore, creative workers need to adapt to the use of AI in the creative industry by equipping themselves with skills and knowledge in operating AI as a collaboration tool. In addition, it is also necessary to consider the ethics of using AI in the creative industry. For example, privacy, copyright, and transparency should be maintained so as not to cause ethical problems such as plagiarism and data biases. This research aims to determine the impact of AI and provide an understanding of its ethical use in the creative industry. This research was conducted using the PRISMA method to collect research papers related to this study. This research also investigates how creative workers deal with the challenges that arise due to the use of AI in the creative industry.

articleTitle: Exploring Educator’s view on Micro-credentials : A Text Mining Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: Micro-credentials have emerged as a promising approach to address the evolving needs of learners and employers in the 21st-century job market. This study aims to investigate educators' perceptions of micro-credentials using a text mining analysis. The study draws on a systematic review of the literature that identifies the opportunities and challenges of micro-credentials. The analysis explores themes related to the meaning and conception of micro-credentials in higher education, as well as the perceived benefits and challenges of implementing them. The findings suggest that while educators recognize the potential of micro-credentials to increase access to education and better align learning outcomes with industry needs, they also express concerns about issues such as the challenge to pursue micro-credentials. The study concludes with implications for policy, practice, and future research on the evolving landscape of micro-credentials in higher education.

articleTitle: Systematic Literature Review on Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis: Insights from Community Reports
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: This systematic literature review examines the utilization of datasets, methodologies, and evaluation metrics in Aspect-Based Sentiment Analysis (ABSA) across 44 scholarly publications. Our analysis identifies prevailing trends in dataset selection, with Twitter and TripAdvisor being the most frequently used sources due to their rich and diverse content. We categorize the various algorithms, ranging from lexicon-based approaches like VADER to advanced machine learning and deep learning models such as SVM and BERT. Standard evaluation metrics, including accuracy, F1-Score, precision, and recall, are analyzed to understand how performance is assessed. The review highlights a shift towards deep learning and hybrid models, reflecting recent technological advancements. Our findings offer a comprehensive overview of the current state of ABSA research, identifying existing gaps and providing insights for future studies to enhance the effectiveness of sentiment analysis techniques.

articleTitle: Predicting National Rice Production Using XGBoost Method Based Hyperparameter Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: The increasing population has an impact on increasing food needs, and increasing rice production is a top priority in human resource development. Indonesia has extensive agricultural land but still imports from other Southeast Asian countries, and the government has taken anticipation through surveys and observations at strategic points using technology. Therefore, this research aims to find a machine learning model to predict rice production in Indonesia with the smallest MAPE. The method used is XGBoost with Grid Search hyperparameters for time series forecasting models, Grid Search is used to find the best parameters to increase accuracy. Prediction results can be used as suggestions or to help make national policies to achieve food self-sufficiency. This research uses rice production data from the Ministry of Agriculture in the period 1970-2022. The results show that XGBoost performs well with a MAPE of 7.43% on training data. Moreover, when the Grid Search hyperparameter is used, it produces a MAPE of 6.73%, which increases the performance.

articleTitle: Organic Waste Management Information System based on SCM and ERP
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: The proper management of the growing waste in Semarang city is essential. A solution to this issue involves implementing an information system approach for waste management. This research aims to (1) build information system based on supply chain management which show organic waste management; (2) build information system based on Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) using Odoo which show waste deposits and pick-up process. The handling and management of organic waste have been effectively mapped in this study, demonstrating community behavior through the supply chain flows from upstream to downstream. Information system of organic waste management are build based on SCM and ERP- Odoo. The results of The information system includes various aspects like the kinds of products manufactured, services offered, and supply chain surveys and flows. By utilizing information systems on the www.produkorganik.id website, it is anticipated that it will aid in addressing issues related to waste management and disposal.

articleTitle: Study of Community Event Introduction Service for Promoting In-Home Elderly Social Participation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: Currently, the proportion of elderly population to the total population in Japan is the highest in the world, and the proportion of elderly population is expected to continue to rise in the future. Also, the proportion of elderly people living alone is increasing year by year, and the proportion of lonely and isolated elderly people is increasing. In such a situation, our research group is developing a virtual agent (VA) listening service to listen to the daily lives of elderly people at home. However, this service lacked functionality to engage users in social activities, so there was a challenge in promoting user social participation. Hence, in this study, we proposed and implemented a "Community Event Introduction Service" to promote social participation of elderly people at home by allowing them to learn about community events while interacting with virtual agent. As a result, we were able to implement a service to propose and remind community events through the Virtual Agent Listening Service, promoting social participation of elderly people at home. In the future, we plan to evaluate the Community Event Introduction Service based on the results of long-term evaluation experiments and implement a function to estimate preferences from the dialogue content of the elderly.

articleTitle: The Impact of POE-LIFE and the Usage of Artificial Intelligence on Students’ Mental Health and Authenticity at Bina Nusantara University
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: Emotion is something that cannot be explained by logic as it is what humans will feel depending on certain situations as each situation can trigger certain emotions. Some emotions need more effort to manage, such as anger, sadness, and other negative emotions. One of the efforts is to express their emotions through literature. POE-LIFE is a developed app to be used as a platform for students to express their emotions through poems, it is also completed with an Artificial Intelligence (AI) function to help students with their poems. The objectives are to know the contributions of POE-LIFE in helping students manage their sadness and anger, to discover the reason(s) behind student’s comfortableness in using AI or not using AI when they are writing poems in POE-LIFE, and to find out the reason of the loss of authenticity when students use AI’s help when writing the poems. The methods used are qualitative and quantitative research methods by analyzing the reasons provided by the participants through the surveys as well as measuring the number of students picking certain answers. The results are that POE-LIFE did help students relieved their emotions, but it is not enough; Most students are quite comfortable in using AI as it can provide ideas for them, but there are still some who did not like to use AI in making poem; and AI did somehow make some students feel like they lose their authenticity if they used the ideas provided by the AI.

articleTitle: Gardening Simulator Based on L-System Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: This paper presents a gardening simulator that leverages the L-System algorithm to procedurally generate realistic plant models. The simulator provides a virtual environment for users to create and interact with digital gardens, offering an engaging and immersive experience. The L-System, a formal grammar introduced by Aristid Lindenmayer, is used to model plant growth patterns, including the formation of branches, leaves, and stems. This approach allows for the semi-automatic creation of diverse plant structures, enhancing realism without the need for extensive manual modeling. The simulator is implemented using Unity, integrating 3D models and texture mapping to produce visually accurate plants. The paper discusses the theoretical foundation of L-Systems, their application in procedural generation, and compares various methods for creating plant models, including traditional rule-based methods and 3D scanning. The resulting simulator aims to make the joy of gardening accessible to a wider audience, including those in urban areas or with physical limitations, while also serving as an educational tool for teaching plant biology and growth processes.

articleTitle: Analyzing Customer Satisfaction Using Chatbots in the Indonesian Banking Sector
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: Chatbot is a technology used to provide chat services to perform a function or convey information via voice or text. Currently, chatbots are widely used in various industries, including the banking sector. The purpose of this research is to analyze the level of customer satisfaction with chatbot services in the banking sector and determine their impact on customer retention and loyalty. Research results from a survey of 385 respondents who actively use chatbot services from various banks show that the majority of customers are satisfied with the availability and responsiveness of chatbots. However, some technical and interactive aspects are considered to need improvement. In summary, chatbots have contributed positively to customer satisfaction. Therefore, ongoing improvements are needed to ensure chatbots remain relevant and meet customer expectations in the future.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence in Massive Open Online Course: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs) are becoming one of today's most widely used learning methods where people can quickly get good quality courses for free. With the help of artificial intelligence, MOOCs are becoming more significant and more effective. AI can monitor user patterns and performance based on the feedback they provide. This research aims to see how attached AI is to MOOCs and the reciprocity they get. Of the 175 studies discovered by the authors during this study, 27 were used as primary references. Researchers use a Systematic literature Review with two research questions: What is the benefit of AI implementation in MOOCs? What are the features of AI in MOOCs? The Researchers believe this paper can further improve performance and effectiveness in the existing MOOC learning system. This research paper explores the relationship between Artificial Intelligence and MOOCs.

articleTitle: Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) in Banking: Users’ Website Usability Experience and Self-Confidence
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: The Human-Computer Interaction (HCI) technologies have brought about metamorphic changes in the banking system. This study aims to examine the users' website usability experience and self-confidence while using banking website, an integral component to HCI. The banking website usability experience was measured on the aspects such as ease of use, efficiency, learnability, error prevention and recovery, accessibility, assistance and guidance, and transaction flow. The assessment of self-confidence involved measuring the users' trust in website security, their sense of control and autonomy, and their perception of website reliability. Furthermore, the study also examined the relationship between users' usability experience and their level of self-confidence when navigating a banking website. The data from 154 respondents was collected through an online survey. Measures of central tendency and parametric tests were used to analyse and test the study hypotheses. The results showed significant differences in the users’ usability experiences and self-confidence levels in relation to the interaction with banking website. Also, the study confirmed a significant relationship between user usability experience and self-confidence level. These study findings offer valuable insights for the banking industry which may help them in enhancing the users’ interaction and system design for ultimately increasing the users’ engagement.

articleTitle: Daing Inside: Development of an Automatic Arduino-based Fish Dryer with Hybrid Power Source
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: The development of the Daing Inside (DI) dryer serves as a transformative solution that effectively addresses the challenges posed by conventional fish drying. The device is programmed to automatically halt the drying process once it reaches its preset target moisture content, using DHT22 and weight sensors, and is powered by a hybrid solar and AC source. The testing of the DI Dryer took place at Tanauan School of Fisheries, at Brgy. Ambulong, Tanauan City, Batangas, on June 26-30, 2023. Forty pieces of Sardinella Tawilis, with lengths ranging from 10 to 12 cm and weights varying between 11 to 17 grams were dried at temperatures maintained at 55°C, 60°C, and 65°C. In comparison, open-sun drying took 33 hours and 21 minutes at a rate of 0.165 g/min. The data reveals a strong negative correlation (-0.9008) between fish weight change and drying time, indicating an inverse relationship. Using 9-point hedonic scale, the survey evaluated dried sample sensory qualities through stratified random sampling among vendors, consumers, and instructors.Notably, the DI dryer set at 65°C outperformed Open-sun drying, proving to be an efficient and effective method for drying fish. The findings highlight the importance of automation and temperature control in achieving both efficiency and good sensory qualities, paving the way for improved drying practices in the fish processing industry.

articleTitle: Frequency Stability Analysis in IEEE 30 Bus Power System Due to Large Load Addition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: Electrical energy is included in the primary needs that also play a role in supporting production activities for industrial consumers and supporting consumer activities in the household environment. However, in the process of fulfilling the need for electrical power, it is necessary to maintain a stable electrical power system at all times. Stability in the electrical power system can be seen through the frequency value. This study aims to determine the response to improving frequency stability in the electrical power system after the addition of the load. This is reviewed from the change in response frequency after a change in load. The design in this study begins with the creation of a line diagram of the IEEE 30 Bus system using ETAP software. Furthermore, in the simulation there are 9 scenarios, namely the addition of a load of 5% of the total load, the addition of a load of 8% of the total load and the addition of a load of 10% of the total load. Where each additional load has 3 conditions, namely the addition of a load on the swing bus, the addition of a load on the 132 kV bus load and the addition of a load on the 33 kV bus load. After that, the frequency stability response on the bus was seen. The results of the study showed that there was a fluctuation in frequency when there was a change in load. The amount of additional load is directly proportional to the amount of frequency reduction. The greater the additional load, the higher the frequency decrease, conversely the smaller the additional load, the lower the frequency decrease that occurs. In the end, the frequency can reach a stable and normal code.

articleTitle: Analysis on Adaptive Difficulty Adjustment for Player Satisfaction in Game: A Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: The different speeds on players learning speed and game mastering can cause a mismatch between the game’s difficulty and the player's skills, that’ll leading into frustration and loss of interest. This study looks at how Adaptive Difficulty Adjustment (ADA) affects player enjoyment and progression throughout the game. ADA changes the game's difficulty in real-time based on each player's performance and emotions, creating a more personalized and engaging gaming experience. This study uses the systematic literature review (SLR) as the base to examine how ADA system will impact different areas, such as player learning, confidence, engagement, and accessibility for people with physical disabilities. The findings show that ADA boosts player satisfaction by offering challenges that are adjusted over time to match skill levels, which improves player retention and educational results. However, relying too much on ADA system could also hinder long-term skill development. Future studies should aim to improve ADA systems, use advanced AI algorithms, and consider player expectations to make gaming experiences even better.

articleTitle: Filter Gabor and SMOTE Method-Based Convolutional Neural Network for Diabetic Retinopathy Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: Diabetic Retinopathy is a disorder of the retina that occurs in people with diabetes and has an increasing risk with age. To prevent the worst risk of blindness, treatment and early detection of eye fundus images are needed. The problem in the image classification is how the model created can have a better performance value. This research aims to classify fundus images with Gabor and SMOTE filters to improve model performance by improving diabetic retinopathy retinal fundus images. The algorithm employed is deep learning, which is a problem-solving method for computer learning systems that use the concept of hierarchy. Among deep learning algorithms for solving detection or identification problems is the convolutional neural network (CNN). In addition, the Gabor Filter is also used to extract retinal fundus image features and SMOTE to overcome unbalanced datasets. The study results showed that Gabor and SMOTE filters could significantly increase the accuracy value from 40% to 78%. The increase in performance value was influenced by preprocessing, namely image resizing, converting to grayscale, and setting Gabor filter parameters.

articleTitle: Latest Technology and Going Digital in Entrepreneurial Business Models in the Digital Economy Era 2024
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: this research examines the influence of the latest technology and digital strategies in entrepreneurial business models in the digital economy era of 2024. The main objective of this research is to understand how the application of the latest technology and digital strategies can increase the competitiveness and sustainability of micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in Indonesia. Quantitative methods were used by analyzing data from 408 respondents who were owners or managers of MSMEs who had implemented digital technology and strategies in their businesses. The research results show that the use of the latest technology such as e-commerce, digital marketing, and digital customer service significantly improves customer performance and satisfaction. The practical implication of this research is the importance of MSMEs adopting digital technology and strategies to remain competitive in an increasingly competitive digital era. This research contributes to the understanding of how digital technology and strategies can support the growth and sustainability of MSMEs in an ever-evolving digital economy.

articleTitle: Underwater Image Enhancement Based on Color Compensation and White Balance
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: Ensuring color accuracy is essential when processing underwater images of coral reefs. These images often suffer from color distortion and blurring due to absorption and scattering. Current trends in underwater color correction focus on mitigating these distortions, as well as addressing non-uniform illumination that leads to artifacts and reduced visibility and contrast. Effective techniques include color compensation for the red channel alone or both the red and blue channels simultaneously. On the color compensated image, the Grayworld and CLAHE methods were applied to compare the results. Evaluations using PSNR, UCIQE, and UIQM metrics confirm that such color compensation techniques significantly enhance the quality of underwater images. It was found that grayworld is able to restore the original color for greenish and yellowish images, while CLAHE can improve dull images.

articleTitle: Professional Camera VS. Smartphone Camera: A Comparison Of Image Quality In A Low-Budget Production Of The Short Film "Pale Moon"
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: The quality of images in film is typically associated with the use of professional cameras and equipment, which can be cost-prohibitive. This study, however, aims to contribute to the field of low-budget filmmaking by comparing a professional camera with a smartphone camera. We examine the extent of the resulting impact and the image quality of a short film entitled "Pale Moon." This research also challenges the assumption that a professional camera or equipment always delivers the best results. Focusing on the pre-production stage, which involves the selection of tools and cameras, and the production stage, which is the execution stage, we demonstrate that the low-budget filmmaking method can still maintain the visual richness of a film. Furthermore, this method can also reduce a film's budget, increasing its efficiency. Therefore, this film and method can be a significant reference for filmmakers or film students, providing them with valuable insights into creating high-quality films on a minimal budget.

articleTitle: Evaluation Of Time Series Forecasting Techniques For Air Quality Prediction: Case Study of NO2 Levels
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: Air quality is an important factor for human life, as a decrease in air quality has a major impact on human health. Nitrogen dioxide (NO2) is one of the main pollutants that has a direct effect on human health. This study assesses the performance of three models for time series forecasting, namely AutoRegressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA), eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) in predicting NO2 concentration. The data used is air quality data from Beijing over the period 2013 to 2024. The research methodology includes data pre-processing steps to address missing values and reduce noise. Afterwards, ARIMA, XGBoost and LSTM models are applied, with the most maximized parameters selected through a cross-validation process. The XGBoost model based on the test results is the model with the best performance among other models, evidenced by the lowest prediction error values (RMSE, MAPE, MAE). The ARIMA and LSTM models, although providing good results, are still below the performance of XGBoost, XGBoost is able to capture fluctuations in NO2 concentration more accurately. This finding suggests that XGBoost is superior in modeling the complexity of air quality time series data. With the results obtained, it is expected to contribute to the development of better air quality prediction strategies and support more informed decision making for public health improvement.

articleTitle: Image Improvement of Underwater Objects Using the Lucy-Richardson Method with the White Balancing Technique with the Gray World Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: Underwater object images have dark and poor image quality due to the depth of the captured image object. Image quality is significantly influenced by illumination. This research uses the Lucy-Richardson method to improve image quality by utilizing knowledge of the degradation process to restore the original image. Meanwhile, the image processing technique, the Lucy-Richardson Method with the White Balancing Technique with the Gray World Model algorithm, sharpens certain features in the object image. The Peak Signal to Noise Ratio (PNSR) is employed to evaluate the research's results, and the results provided can offer solutions to the problems above.

articleTitle: Gamification in the Marketplace for Gen Z: Determinants Using Gamified Learning Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: Gamification is the process of incorporating game design aspects into non-gaming products or services to enhance usage and provide more long-term effects. The implementation of gamification in diverse practical focus areas necessitates the application and adaptation of the gamification theoretical idea to technological breakthroughs and their application. The goal of this study is to examine the determinants of gamification in the marketplace using gamified learning theory. This research takes a quantitative approach, utilizing SEM-PLS modeling and the SmartPLS 4.0 analytic tool. Participants from Generation Z were employed for this study. This group is recognized for its tendency to become readily bored and to move around while utilizing a product. According to the findings of this study, varying the intensity of recommendations to other people can demonstrate that the output does not only stop at the outcomes of playing, such as the acquisition of coins or other rewards, but also extends to the act of recommending to others. This is consistent with the game's features, which include the ability to invite friends to help finish objectives. This study has theoretical significance for enhancing differentiated learning theory. In practice, the findings of this study highlight the importance of consistently designing instructional features and content to keep students' attention. The research's flaws stem from the usage of limited game elements and the participants' background profile, which was ignored in favor of ignoring their game experience.

articleTitle: Comparison of ResNet & VGGNet for Traffic Sign Image Quality in Nighttime
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: Traffic signs are one of the important road equipment facilities that inform road users about regulations and instructions visually. Currently, an automated Traffic Sign Recognition (TSR) system is being developed and applied to advanced driver systems (ADAS) so that road users can be safe and secure while on the road. This study explores the application of Histogram Equalization (HE) to improve the visibility of traffic signs in low-lighting conditions, using the deep learning architectures ResNet50 and VGG19. This study aims to evaluate the impact of HE on the performance of these models in recognizing traffic signs. The experimental results show that on the ResNet50 architecture, HE maintains the test accuracy at around 92%, while on VGG19, HE improves the test accuracy from 89.62% to 92.54%. These findings are relevant for Traffic Sign Recognition (TSR) systems, which are an important component of Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS). By improving traffic sign recognition accuracy under low illumination conditions, Histogram Equalization contributes to improved road safety through more reliable and responsive ADAS systems, which rely on TSR to provide critical information to drivers.

articleTitle: Optimizing Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients for Improved Robot Speech Command Recognition Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: In this study, we optimized Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (MFCC) for speech recognition. The experiment involved recording eight words by one hundred individuals with tempo, pitch, duration, resolution, and speech clarity variations. The results showed that the image's shape for each word remained consistent despite variations in pronunciation, confirming that MFCC is an effective method for feature extraction in speech recognition, particularly in robotic environments. Using logarithms in MFCC clarifies minor differences in amplitude scale, resulting in sharper contours and more visible details. This study recommends optimizing MFCC parameters, testing on larger datasets, and applying the method in various operational conditions to enhance its reliability in the future

articleTitle: Explainable AI in Cybersecurity: A Comprehensive Framework for enhancing transparency, trust, and Human-AI Collaboration
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: Explainable AI (XAI) is transforming cybersecurity through increased openness, reliability, and teamwork among human analysts and AI tools. This comprehensive framework explores the application of XAI techniques like SHAP, LIME, and EBM to address the challenges of explainability and trustworthiness in AI-driven cybersecurity solutions. This paper tackles the core issue of limited clarity and explainability in conventional AI models for cybersecurity. This opacity can impede trust-building and productive teamwork between humans and AI systems.As a solution, this paper suggests incorporating Explainable AI (XAI) methodologies into cybersecurity structures. This would offer understandable explanations about how AI systems reach their conclusions. This empowers cybersecurity professionals to understand, validate, and effectively respond to cyber threats. The evaluation of XAI techniques against traditional cybersecurity models reveals superior performance, particularly in intrusion detection systems (IDS), phishing detection, incident response, vulnerability assessment, threat intelligence, anomaly detection, malware detection, SOAR, and user behavior analytics (UBA). This research not only strengthens cybersecurity defenses but also fosters a deeper understanding of AI's role in safeguarding digital ecosystems.

articleTitle: The Influence of Social Media on Voter Behavior, Public Opinion, and Partisan Tendencies during Election Campaigns in Indonesia: Systematic Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: In the current digital era, social media has become a crucial tool in obtaining information. Social media is also used by presidential and vice-presidential candidates to build a positive image, spread vision and mission, political messages, and interact with the public. Social media provides opportunities for voters to be actively involved in various political discussions and debates. Through social media, voters can share views, express support or differences of opinion, and obtain information regarding candidates who will take part in the election. These things create a scheme that increasingly influences a voter's political views. The purpose of this research is to examine how social media can influence the election process and how it affects public opinion, the tendency of people to support certain candidates. In this research, the authors want to conduct a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) by analyzing information based on many previous studies related to this topic. In general, we concluded that social media does have a significant influence in shaping voter behavior, public opinion and tendencies during the election period.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-based Malware Detection on Android Operating System using AdaBoost Algorithm and ReliefF Feature Selection Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: Technological advancements occur rapidly from year to year. Currently, we experience the benefits of this rapid technological development, including the widespread use of smartphones in our daily lives. However, without robust security measures, smartphones can lead to losses for users and associated individuals. Additionally, as malware evolves, detecting it becomes increasingly challenging. Therefore, AI-based malware detection methods are essential to replace conventional fingerprint-based approaches that struggle to identify new types of malwares. In this research, we explore several stages: data collection, pre-processing, modeling, and evaluation. Our focus is on identifying optimal combinations of pre-processing and modeling methods to achieve high performance in Android malware detection. Specifically, we implement three feature selection methods, such as X<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (Chi-Square), Information Gain, and ReliefF, in the pre-processing stage. Similarly, in the modeling stage, we employ three classification algorithms, namely: Random Forest, AdaBoost, and Gradient Boosting, to learn patterns from the data. Our most effective solution is the combination of the AdaBoost classifier with the ReliefF feature selection method, achieving 99.4% accuracy and F1-Score.

articleTitle: Increasing Production Capacity with IoT-based Floating Net Cage Technology for Erorejo Wadaslintang Freshwater Fishermen
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: In the last decade, the cultivation of floating net cages for freshwater fishermen in the Wadaslintang reservoir in Erorejo has grown significantly. It is currently one of the contributors to freshwater aquaculture production in Wonosobo Regency. This research aims to implement IoT-based portable floating net cage technology to increase the production capacity of freshwater fisheries in Erorejo, Wadaslintang. This research focuses on red Tilapia, striped catfish, and freshwater milkfish. We analyzed the characteristics of fish seeds, cultivation technology, feed supply, and marketing. We used simple random sampling with 50 fishermen respondents in the Wadaslintang reservoir. We implemented three portable floating net cages for four months. The research showed that of the 1,340 floating net cages, 77.5% were used for red tilapia cultivation, and the remaining 20% of striped catfish were used for freshwater milkfish trials. The average production of red Tilapia is 106.74 kg/day/fisherman, striped catfish 16.26 kg/day/fisherman, and freshwater milkfish has not been recorded. Using IoT-based portable floating net cages showed an average increase of 21% in the production of red Tilapia and 18.5% in striped catfish. Future research must examine the reservoir area's spatial suitability with the productivity level.

articleTitle: Narratives from the Field: Big Data's Role in Digital Marketing Transformation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: In today's digitally driven landscape, Big Data is revolutionizing digital marketing practices across industries, catering to businesses of all sizes. Despite its transformative potential, a significant gap exists in understanding how effectively businesses leverage Big Data analytics to optimize their marketing strategies. This study aims to fill this gap by providing a comprehensive exploration of the profound influence of Big Data on the digital marketing ecosystem. The study employs a mixed-method approach, combining qualitative research methodology—reviewing secondary data from case studies and business reports—with quantitative analysis of real-world digital marketing campaigns. The study unveils the pivotal role of data-driven decision-making and real-time information processing in optimizing digital marketing efforts. The findings highlight that Big Data assists firms in developing optimized pricing strategies, enhancing both sales and profitability. Businesses investing in Big Data and advanced analytics experience substantial returns, improved productivity, and sales effectiveness. Personalization driven by Big Data significantly boosts sales and delivers high returns on marketing investments. Furthermore, Customer Lifecycle Management (CLM) powered by Big Data aids in acquiring new customers, developing existing ones, and retaining valuable clients, thereby further increasing profitability. The study also underscores the importance of sentiment analysis facilitated by Big Data, helping marketers understand consumer attitudes and preferences, improving product quality, and identifying new business opportunities. The implications of this study are significant for businesses seeking to remain competitive in the ever-evolving digital marketing landscape. Companies leveraging Big Data can achieve a competitive edge through enhanced targeting, personalization, and customer engagement. However, adopting robust data privacy and ethical standards is crucial for maintaining consumer trust and regulation compliance.

articleTitle: Fine-Grained Sentiment Classification of Public Opinion on Electric Cars in Indonesia Using IndoBERT
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: This research aims to analyze public sentiment towards electric cars in Indonesia using the IndoBERT model. Data were collected from social media platforms, especially Twitter or X, and processed using the IndoBERT Model for Indonesian-language public opinion. The dataset consists of 1,087 tweets, which were preprocessed and labelled into five sentiment categories: very positive, positive, neutral, negative, and very negative. According to the study's findings, the majority of public opinion in Indonesia is neutral (70.45%), then positive (21.65%), negative (6.13%), very positive (1.49%), and very negative (0.28%). Although the overall trend is positive, there are concerns about the charging infrastructure and the price of electric cars. The enhanced IndoBERT model achieved outstanding performance, with accuracy increasing from 74% in the first epoch to 80% in the fifth epoch and F1 score increasing from 0.83 to 0.89. These findings provide valuable insights for policymakers and manufacturers in supporting the adoption of electric cars in Indonesia

articleTitle: Cybersecurity Data Analytics System Success: An Exploratory Study on U.S Government Agencies
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: United States government organizations are compelled to comply with federal, state, and local cybersecurity regulations by law. This includes robust reactive and proactive measures to protect against the ever-increasing cybersecurity threat landscape. Given the intense government regulatory mandates, cybersecurity data analytics systems play an important role in uncovering patterns, optimizing resource allocation, and stimulating innovation. This includes deploying cybersecurity data analytics systems (CDAS) to detect and counteract malicious activities proactively. As such, there is a need to empirically examine the organizational factors that influence the success of CDAS within U.S. government agencies. This study assesses the impact of Top Management Support (TMS), Internal Processes (IP), and Learning and Growth (LAG) from a competitive advantages perspective based on the resource-based view (RBV) theory. This study gathered survey data from cybersecurity and IT professionals and analyzed the results using a second-generation multivariate analysis technique. The findings indicate that TMS, IP, and LAG significantly influence Cybersecurity Data Analytics Systems Success (CDASS). The practical implications of this study promote the need for top management support, efficient internal processes, and ongoing learning and growth initiatives to increase a CDA system’s implementation success, thereby improving the cybersecurity posture of U.S. government agencies and, in turn, improving the state of U.S. national cybersecurity preparedness.

articleTitle: Implementation of a Mixed Triple Logistic Map and the BB84 Quantum Key Distribution for Secure Image Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: In the digital era, data communication security is one of the main challenges. This research proposes a new method for secure image communication, which is a mixed triple logistic map and BB84 quantum key distribution. This approach combines the strengths of classical and quantum cryptographic systems to improve security. BB84 quantum key distribution protocol for securely distributing encryption keys. The resulting key is then processed into a hash value using the SHA-256 algorithm. These hash values are converted into ASCII values, which are used to generate three key sequences using the modified logistic map. The three key sequences are combined to form a keystream used in image encryption. Several security metrics are used to evaluate encryption security, including entropy, the Chi-Square test, and pixel correlation. The analysis results show that the encrypted image has an entropy close to eight. In addition, all chi-square values smaller than 293 indicate a uniform distribution. The correlation of nearby pixels in the encrypted image is also very low, where all values are less than 0.01, which indicates the loss of local patterns in the encrypted image. These results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively secures image communications, providing high security and resistance to conventional and quantum cryptographic attacks.

articleTitle: Framework to increase the level of customer satisfaction in telecommunication services in Peru using TQM and Business Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: In recent years, technological advancement and the COVID-19 pandemic have increased internet consumption worldwide, making it essential for daily activities such as work, studies and leisure. Therefore, an efficient Internet service is necessary, but many Internet service providers are facing an increase in customer dissatisfaction that leads to long-term losses of customers and money for these companies [1]. For this reason, a continuous improvement framework based on Business Intelligence is proposed that will have the main objective of increasing the level of customer satisfaction in telecommunications services in Peru, which will be measured by performance indicators. A model based on the four phases of TQM was applied: Plan, Do, Check and Act. In the Planning phase, areas for improvement are identified, in the Do phase the improvements are implemented, in Verify the results are collected and analyzed, and in Act the results are reviewed to adapt and standardize the proposed improvements, finally a plan is implemented to provide continuity to the proposed model, based on ITIL 4. The main metric The results showed 71.67% based on the SLA performance algorithm, which demonstrates an improvement in the performance of the company's technical assistance service, which is currently 70%.

articleTitle: Enhancing Driver Drowsiness Detection through GMM-Optimized CLAHE
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: This research investigates the integration of Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) with Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) to enhance image contrast, specifically for driver drowsiness detection based on facial images. Traditional CLAHE employs a fixed clip limit for contrast enhancement, which may not adapt well to varying image characteristics. To address this, the proposed CLAHE+GMM method dynamically determines the optimal contrast limit using GMM clustering. This approach aims to achieve more adaptive and effective contrast enhancement. The evaluation metrics used in this study include Mean Squared Error (MSE), Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR), Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR), and computation time, providing a comprehensive assessment of the methods' performance. Experimental results indicate that employing 2 clusters in CLAHE+GMM significantly improves MSE, PSNR, and SNR, demonstrating the method's effectiveness. Visual histogram comparisons and sample images further validate that CLAHE+GMM with 2 clusters closely aligns with the grayscale base image, ensuring stable and consistent enhancement. In conclusion, the CLAHE+GMM approach, particularly with 2 clusters, offers a promising solution for enhancing image contrast in driver drowsiness detection applications, contributing to improved safety in driving environments.

articleTitle: Lymphoma sub-type classification using DenseNet 169-based Transfer Learning Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: Lymphoma is a serious disease with significant potential complications, including heart disease, lung disease, and increased susceptibility to infections due to immune system suppression. This study aims to classify lymphoma cells using a digital pathology dataset comprising three types: Chronic Lymphocytic Leukemia (CLL), Follicular Lymphoma (FL), and Mantle Cell Lymphoma (MCL), with 113, 139, and 122 images, respectively. Image augmentation techniques were applied to address the limited dataset, resizing the images to 40% from the original 1388 x 1040 pixels. The classification was performed using a deep learning approach with transfer learning, specifically employing the DenseNet169 model from TensorFlow. The DenseNet169 model, initialized with ImageNet weights and optimized with specific parameters, achieved an accuracy of 99.1%, surpassing previous research by 0.4%. The study demonstrates that image augmentation, combined with transfer learning, effectively enhances classification accuracy in the context of limited datasets.

articleTitle: Exploring the Impact of Image Downscaling Algorithms on Color Perception
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: Several image downscaling algorithms have been developed over the years, yet their impact on color perception after downscaling has not been thoroughly investigated. This study conducts various experiments to evaluate traditional and modern image downscaling algorithms and their effects on color preservation. Using the adapted method of Quantitative Color Pattern Analysis (QCPA), we objectively measure each algorithm's performance in maintaining color perception. The algorithms compared include Bicubic Interpolation, Lanczos Resampling, Seam Carving, and Rapid Detail-Preserving Image Downscaling (RDPID) using the Imagenette and DIV2K datasets. Evaluation metrics encompass average color histogram similarity, dominant color shifts, and color scatter plots. Results reveal varying degrees of color information loss among the algorithms, with Bicubic Interpolation and RDPID showing superior color fidelity compared to Seam Carving. For the Imagenette dataset, average color histogram similarity between the original and downscaled images is 78.9% for Bicubic Interpolation, 75.8% Lanczos Resampling, 77.6% for RDPID, and 20.8% for Seam Carving. For the DIV2K dataset, the similarities are 65.7% for Bicubic Interpolation, 64.7% for RDPID, and 48.8% for Seam Carving. This research highlights the extent of color information loss due to the downscaling process across the chosen algorithms. Future studies should explore additional algorithms and assess their performance across diverse datasets and applications, enhancing our understanding of color information loss in image downscaling and its impact on computer vision tasks.

articleTitle: Scoping Review Of Sign Language Recognition: An Analysis of MediaPipe Framework and Deep Learning Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: This scoping review aims to examine the research progression in computer vision about sign language recognition using MediaPipe and deep learning. The following steps are carried out, identifying the research question, Identifying relevant research, selecting studies, organizing the data, and compiling, summarizing, and presenting the findings. The analysis is based on 209 articles published from 2019 to the first quarter of 2024. The findings address two quantitative research questions about the number of titles, cites per year, and number of authors, ultimately concluding that there is a growing momentum in Sign Language Recognition with MediaPipe research, signaling a transition from its initial phase to a more sophisticated and established stage. In a qualitative research question about deep learning techniques, we use filtered methods to analyze the text of articles and search for keywords related to specific deep learning techniques. From 209 articles, we narrowed 38 articles found to analyze, and the result is the most used technique MediaPipe for feature extractor and Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) for temporal features with different configuration layers.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of the Influence Factors of Webrooming and Showrooming on Consumer’s Final Purchase Decisions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: As technology and information advance, people find it increasingly convenient to perform searches and transactions online. This trend became even more pronounced during the COVID-19 pandemic when individuals significantly limited their physical movements. Consequently, a new phenomenon, known as cross-channel shopping behaviors, emerged. Consumers now prefer a combination of channels, such as showrooming and webrooming. The research esplores how Brand Image, Price, Promotion, Information Accuracy, Perceived Risk, and Product Variety influence webrooming and showrooming on consumers' final purchase decisions. This study utilized a quantitative data collection method by distributing an online questionnaire to consumers who engage in webrooming and showrooming behaviors. The data was analyzed using the Structural Equation Model - Partial Least Squares method, with SmartPLS 4 software. This research examines consumer behavior in determining purchasing decisions through webrooming and showrooming. The findings show that brand image, promotion, information accuracy, perceived risk, and product variety have a significant effect on webrooming purchase decisions. Then, promotion, information accuracy, and product variety have a significant effect on showrooming purchase decisions. While price was found to have insignificant results on the webrooming purchase decision and brand image, price, and perceived risk had insignificant results on the showrooming purchase decisions. Thus, business people are advised to be able to adapt in facing the phenomenon of omnichannel customers to meet their preferences and remain competitive in this digital era.

articleTitle: Maturity Model for PCI SLC Compliance for Peruvian Software Development Companies based on CMMI
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: In the banking sector, the demand for digital payments has grown by 150% in the last three years, exposing sensitive data to risks such as theft and impersonation. To mitigate these risks, banks seek to improve their infrastructure and applications, but the IT industry in Peru has decreased by 3% annually due to incidents with products that do not meet international standards, weakening customer confidence. Therefore, a maturity model is proposed to verify compliance with Payment Card Industry Secure Software Lifecycle (PCI SLC) regulations in Peruvian companies that develop software. The model consists of 3 stages: (1) analysis, (2) design and (3) validation. In (1), information security standards and methodologies for the development of the proposal are evaluated. In (2), the model was designed under the six phases of the "De Bruin" methodology. In (3), the model was validated through a survey with experts and a case study, to know the effectiveness of the maturity model when evaluating security controls in a software. After having deployed the maturity model proposed in the case study, it was found to be at a "defined" maturity level, since it obtained a maturity score of 0.68. This result was corroborated by the case study through the detailed analysis of the maturity scores obtained for each phase of the software life cycle.

articleTitle: Regression-Based Exploration of Factors Influencing Movie Profits
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: Accurate box office prediction is crucial for managing financial risks in film production. The internet has transformed consumer behavior, affecting marketing strategies. Critical online reviews, more than early revenue, predict a film's profit, while establishing film critics as the predictors. Hence, this study investigates the intricate relationship between ratings and movies profit. While also finding the best model to predict those variables. This research was conducted through a comprehensive process encompassing data collection and processing, feature selection, prediction modeling, and a detailed discussion of the conducted analysis. Several manual interventions were applied to the data to support further discoveries and analysis in this research. These interventions were carried out based on a solid foundation to enhance the depth of exploration and understanding within the study. The findings reveal that the random forest regression emerged as the most effective in this study, achieving the Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 768.40. Leveraging a dataset of 500 movies from Kaggle.com, incorporating critics' ratings from RottenTomatoes.com. Through this research, industry professionals not only enhance their understanding but also identify factors that can be considered to increase a movie’s revenue.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: Analysis of the Influence of Brand Image on Behavioral Intent: A Study on Social Media Advertising and Sales Promotion Content for Local Skincare Products
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: Social media is now a crucial part of business and marketing, especially in the local skincare industry. This study looks at how brand image affects consumer behavior in response to social media ads and promotions for local skincare products. It focuses on Instagram and TikTok users in Indonesia and explores the relationship between social media content, brand image, and consumer behavior. The research gathered data through an online survey of local skincare consumers active on social media. Using purposive sampling, 371 respondents from the Jabodetabek area who frequently use social media were selected. The data was analyzed with Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) and Partial Least Squares (PLS). The goal is to help local skincare companies build consumer trust with effective social media marketing by identifying key factors that drive online purchase intentions. The study found that social media ads and promotions significantly enhance brand image and encourage positive consumer behavior. This research contributes to the understanding of social media communication and branding by highlighting the important role of brand image.

articleTitle: SVM-Classified FaceNet and Eigenface Models under Lighting and Occlusion Variations for Face Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
abstract: Emotional interactions between teachers and learners are essential in educational settings. This study aimed to help teachers recognize and respond to learners' emotions effectively by proposing a suitable face recognition system for use in learner emotion recognition systems. The research compared two models, FaceNet with Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Eigenface with SVM, using a single sample per learner. The results show that FaceNet and SVM models performed better, achieving almost perfect accuracy of 98%, while Eigenface only reached 84%. Under various lighting conditions, the FaceNet and SVM models maintained a high accuracy of 90%, whereas Eigenface reached only 9%.
